title: Mise en place

keyPoints.line: we are always on the guest’s side.

read.where: **Service is what we do; hospitality is how it makes the guest feel.** Drawing on the philosophies of **Danny Meyer** (Setting the Table) and **Will Guidara** (Unreasonable Hospitality), this module treats **every table as a conversation**: one where we are **always on the guest’s side**, and where small, personal gestures become the moments guests **remember and retell**.

sections.name: Your station and what you know

keyPoints.line: a prepared server can be, with every guest.
napkins, crumber, wine key, pens, candles.
know it, with ingredients and allergens.

read.bigIdea: Everything in its place before the doors open.
read.where: A prepared server is free to be **fully present** with guests, because nothing pulls attention away from them.

stops.name: Station
stops.text: Glassware and silver **polished and spotless**; linens **pressed**; the side stand stocked with **napkins, crumber, wine key, pens, candles** and water service pieces.

stops.name: Knowledge
stops.text: **Taste the specials.** Know ingredients, **allergens**, the **86 list**, and the wine, cocktail and water offerings well enough to describe them **in a sentence**.

keyPoints.line: your mind and your station between tables.

read.bigIdea: Plan a gesture before the guest arrives.
read.where: Pre-shift is where the evening’s **gestures** get planned, and where you get yourself ready.

stops.name: Pre-shift
stops.text: Review **reservations and guest notes**: **regulars, celebrations, dietary needs and VIPs**, so we can **plan a gesture** before the guest arrives.

stops.name: Self
stops.text: Uniform **pressed**, grooming **immaculate**, **phone away**. **Reset your mind and your station** between every table.

sources: The Art of Table Service: introduction and 1, Mise en Place.
